summary: This is a tadabbur class on Surah Al-Alaq in a mosque in Ramadan. The ustaz presents the Quran as the word of Allah, revealed in Arabic over 23 years and preserved by Allah, then recalls the Hira event and the meaning of ummi. He then reflects on the first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq: reading in the name of the Lord who created, man made from alaq through stages of 40, 40 and 40 days until the soul is breathed in, and four things written: lifespan, provision, deeds and final end. He also explains the Most Generous Lord who taught by the pen, and that people keep learning throughout life. The lecture closes with questions and a quiz.
keyPoints: The Quran was revealed in Arabic over 23 years and Allah protects it from any alteration.
The Prophet SAW could not read because he was ummi, but Jibril delivered the first five verses of Al-Alaq and he memorised them.
The first verse commands reading in the name of the Lord who created, not a lord made by people.
Man was created from alaq, and after 120 days the soul is breathed in and four things are written: lifespan, provision, deeds and final end.
Allah taught man by the pen and people keep learning all their lives.

chapters.title: Opening and the Al-Um Mosque
chapters.summary: The ustaz recalls the history of idols and introduces the Al-Um Mosque, meaning mother, linked to ummi.

chapters.title: The Quran is the word of Allah
chapters.summary: The Quran is Allah's word. It was once written on animal skins and wood, and compiled by Abu Bakr after the Prophet SAW died.

chapters.title: Thirty juz, one hundred and fourteen surahs
chapters.summary: The Quran has 30 juz and 114 surahs, beginning with Al-Fatihah and ending with An-Nas.

chapters.title: Twenty-three years, in Arabic
chapters.summary: The Quran came down bit by bit over 23 years in Arabic and is protected by Allah from change.

chapters.title: How revelation came
chapters.summary: Revelation sometimes came like the sound of a bell, so heavy that a camel knelt or a companion's leg felt like breaking.

chapters.title: The Cave of Hira and the meaning of ummi
chapters.summary: At 39 years 6 months he began to dream and withdrew to the cave, answering I am ummi when told to read.

chapters.title: The Arabs' strong memory
chapters.summary: The Arabs did not read but memorised the lineages of people and of their camels and horses.

chapters.title: Surah 96 and the basmalah
chapters.summary: Every surah starts with Bismillah except At-Tawbah, because it concerns Allah's anger at shirk.

chapters.title: Verse one: read in the name of your Lord
chapters.summary: Read anything but in the name of Allah who created everything, from the greatest to the smallest cell.

chapters.title: Verse two: from alaq
chapters.summary: Allah created man from a clot, and the Rabb is the Lord who creates, owns and sustains.

chapters.title: From earth and alaq to the soul's blowing
chapters.summary: Adam was created from earth, while his children come from alaq. Every 40 days it changes until 120 days when the angel breathes in the soul.

chapters.title: Four things that are written
chapters.summary: When the soul is breathed in Allah writes lifespan, provision, deeds and whether the end is happy or wretched.

chapters.title: Verses three and four: the Most Generous and the pen
chapters.summary: Allah repeats the command to read and mentions His generosity, then teaching by the pen. Writing develops knowledge and Prophet Idris was the first to write.

chapters.title: Verse five: lifelong learning
chapters.summary: Allah taught man what he did not know, so we never stop learning and we write to remember.

chapters.title: Questions about the heart
chapters.summary: Pupils ask about the baby's and mother's hearts, and the ustaz explains the heart and oxygen.

chapters.title: Sirah quiz
chapters.summary: The class closes with a quiz on the idols, the mosque, the Quran and the Prophet's story, with prizes for correct answers.

dalil.context: The ustaz recites and explains the first verse of Surah Al-Alaq.
dalil.translation: Read! In the name of your Lord who created:

dalil.context: He created man from a clinging clot.
dalil.translation: He created manfrom a clinging form.

dalil.context: Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous.
dalil.translation: Read! Your Lord is the Most Bountiful One
who taught by [means of] the pen,

dalil.context: He taught man what he did not know.
dalil.translation: who taught man what he did not know.

dalil.context: The ustaz recites the verse that Ramadan is the month the Quran was sent down.
dalil.translation: It was in the month of Ramadan that the Quran was revealed as guidance for mankind, clear messages giving guidance and distinguishing between right and wrong. So any one of you who is present that month should fast, and anyone who is ill or on a journey should make up for the lost days by fasting on other days later. God wants ease for you, not hardship. He wants you to complete the prescribed period and to glorify Him for having guided you, so that you may be thankful.

The Prophet SAW said man is gathered in the womb forty days as a drop, forty days as a clot, forty days as a lump of flesh, then the angel breathes in the soul and writes provision, lifespan, deeds and whether wretched or happy.
dalil.context: The ustaz cites the Prophet's words on the stages of the embryo. He does not name a narrator or source.

dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW said Allah created Adam from a handful of earth of varied colours, so Adam's children come in different colours and temperaments.
dalil.context: The ustaz relays the Prophet's words on the origin of people's colours and temperaments. He does not name a narrator or source.

people.context: Compiled the Quran after the Prophet SAW died.
Embraced the Prophet SAW three times and delivered the first five verses of Al-Alaq.
Created from earth of varied colours, not from alaq.
Taught by Allah to write with the pen.
His story is mentioned most in the Quran.

sirah.era: The start of revelation: reflecting on Surah Al-Alaq
sirah.summary: This lecture revisits the first revelation at the Cave of Hira and reflects on the first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq.

events.label: Dreams
events.title: True dreams begin
events.desc: At 39 years 6 months he began to dream and seek answers.

events.label: Embrace
events.title: Jibril embraces him
events.desc: The angel embraced him until he could hardly breathe and said read.

events.label: Verses
events.title: The first five verses are delivered
events.desc: The third time Jibril delivered the first verses of Al-Alaq.

lessons.title: Reading in Allah's name
lessons.body: All reading and knowledge should begin with the name of the Lord who created.

lessons.title: The Quran is preserved by Allah
lessons.body: No one can alter a letter, word or surah of the Quran.

lessons.title: Allah creates and sustains
lessons.body: The Rabb is the Lord who creates and keeps sustaining His servant until death.

lessons.title: Reflect on our origin
lessons.body: We come from a clot of nothing, and Allah made us knowing humans.

lessons.title: Lifespan, provision, deeds and end are written
lessons.body: Allah writes four things when the soul is breathed in, but He does not force us and we make our choices.

lessons.title: Giving thanks for blessings
lessons.body: We are given many blessings such as eyes, ears, food and legs to run.

lessons.title: Writing binds knowledge
lessons.body: Writing down what we learn helps us remember it.

lessons.title: Lifelong learning
lessons.body: We never stop learning even when old.
